# MLOW oracle fixtures

The primary oracle is the shipped WhatsApp VoIP wasm. Every primary fixture below is now
regenerated from `synth_mic.raw` through the original encoder/decoder, including intermediate DSP
inputs, outputs and state. There is no recorded call audio or real PII in this corpus.

The synthetic input is generated by `synth_mic_pcm()` in `quality_tests.rs`; its bytes are checked by
`synth_mic_raw_matches_generator`. Regenerate it with `MLOW_GEN_SYNTH=1 cargo test -p wacore
--features voip-mlow --lib regen_synth_mic_raw`. Changing it requires re-deriving the entire corpus.

## Primary corpus and reproducible recipe

The exact derivation lock is
[`mlow.lock.json`](../../../../../tools/oracle-core/specs/mlow.lock.json). The
local [`mlow_derivation.md`](../../../../../agent_docs/mlow_derivation.md)
records function identities, layouts, instruction boundaries and measured fixes.
`Cargo.lock` pins the generic `unwasm-core` analysis and whatspec `wa-store` inputs.
The WhatsApp-specific Wasmtime host and every derivation recipe are local
host-only tools excluded from `default-members`; neither `wacore` nor the
application runtime depends on them.

```sh
cargo xt mlow regenerate --check
# To replace fixtures after an intentional, reviewed oracle change, omit --check.
```

The Rust task builds the tool with locked dependencies, fetches hash-pinned captures when needed,
runs all 11 derivations, verifies every output and selector, assembles the fixtures and packs them.
It runs from any directory; its disposable work stays under `--out` (default `.derive-mlow/wasm`).
`--from-derived DIR` may reuse a previous run only after verifying its complete manifests and output
hashes.
No recipe depends on the old `/tmp` investigation files.

| Capture | Size | SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---|
| `JgwtTQVeWPm` | 10,650,934 B | `97259423aea19cc30c1771478e035105cb0d0e64ab4b0297741b62d01deac8db` |
| `S_ivh1PriOA` | 10,856,103 B | `e55e43babf85e2c0fc76ec65dcb8d47beba0f58b03b135b37a5aaaff7fe70e2f` |

J and S produce identical packets **and PCM** over the full 110-packet 60 ms stream and the
8-packet 120 ms stream. S uses its re-derived allocation/vtable layout: its decoder-init skip flag
is at `attr+1200`, so the old 1184-byte allocation was invalid. The decoder context is created by
`opus_open`; it is not forged to bypass the failure.

| Fixture | Coverage | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `wasm_derived_frames.json` + `wasm_derived_ref.raw` | 110 packets / 110×960 s16le samples; J/S equality | `quality_tests`, `decoder` |
| `wasm_derived_120ms_frames.json` + `wasm_derived_120ms_ref.raw` | 8 packets / 8×1920 samples; J/S equality | `decoder` |
| `wasm_derived_vad.json` | 99 active / 11 inactive packets | `smpl_vad` |
| `wasm_fe.cbor.zst` | 330 windows, F2, R, LPC before/after BWE | `smpl_lpc` |
| `wasm_signal_mode.cbor.zst` | 330 VUV inputs/outputs/states and exact speech-activity probabilities | `smpl_signal_mode`, `smpl_vad` |
| `wasm_pitch.cbor.zst` | 330 pitch inputs/outputs, predictor state and search configuration | `smpl_pitch_enc` |
| `wasm_lsf_quant.cbor.zst` | 330 quantizations, including 219 conditional cases | `smpl_lsf_quant` |
| `wasm_params.cbor.zst` | 330 LSF/pulse/pitch/gain records and complete entropy-context words | `param_decode_match`, `rangecoder` |
| `wasm_gennoise.cbor.zst` | 1320 excitation/noise inputs/outputs and NoiseGenerator states | `smpl_gennoise`, `smpl_celpdec` |
| `wasm_hp_postfilter.cbor.zst` | 330 HP filter inputs/outputs/states | `smpl_harmcomb` |
| `wasm_harm_postfilter.cbor.zst` | 110 harmonic-filter inputs/outputs/states | `smpl_harm_postfilter` |

The stream contains 11×`0x10`, 3×`0x12`, 96×`0x50`. Inactive packets are indices 17–19 and 62–69;
hangover packets are 16, 59 and 61. `0x12` counts as active routing. The explicit `mlow_dtx_off`
spec executes SET_DTX(0), reads GET_DTX()==0 and retains all 220 packet/PCM hashes. The earlier claim
that this pair used DTX enabled was incorrect. DTX comparisons feed every packet through the Rust
decoder before selecting inactive outputs, preserving the reference stream history.

Encoder and decoder from one wasm capture are one source, not independent votes. Rust-vs-wasm
checks coexist with the independent C auditors below. DSP floats use documented tolerances; wire
symbols, RNG state, VAD probabilities and J/S output hashes are exact. The LPC test additionally
checks the solve against the exact oracle autocorrelation for all frames. For ill-conditioned,
near-silent input, FFT-induced coefficient differences must either meet the normal coefficient
bound or imply less than one s16 PCM LSB of prediction error.

The wasm exposed older tuning in the C-derived Rust implementation. The runtime now follows the
shipped values: LPC BWE 0.9985, VUV bias -0.13, pitch previous weight 0.7 and delta weight 0.3,
harmonic feedback 0.4 and strength 0.713. LPC regularization promotes to f64 before adding 1.
The pitch fixture carries the forged encoder's 4-survivor/low-complexity setting; the Rust encoder
retains its 24-survivor budget. C tests explicitly use their historical tuning where it differs.

## Binary packaging and independent C auditors

`cargo xt mlow pack` encodes JSON values as CBOR and zstd. It preserves integers, float types and every numeric
value; an f32 representation is used only when exact. The check compares decompressed CBOR bytes,
so a different zstd version cannot masquerade as changed oracle data. `wasm-fixtures.json` records
artifact hashes/sizes. Rust uses test-only `ciborium` and pure-Rust `ruzstd`; runtime dependencies
and the runtime `.bin` tables are unaffected.

The large legacy JSON and two postfilter RAW files were replaced by compact archives. Their
independent C outputs were not changed to agree with Rust. Regenerate/check those archives with:

```sh
cargo xt mlow pack-legacy --check
```

That recipe reads the immutable historical fixture commit pinned in the Rust task (a full-history
checkout, or fetching that commit, is required). `packed-fixtures.json` records original source
hashes, selected record counts, canonical CBOR hashes and sizes. The C fork behind those historical
outputs is `edgardmessias/opus_mlow@84b076e0809412df22e8a0d26f944610c4a3e40f`; some original dump
harnesses/configurations were lost, so replaying the archived bytes is deliberately distinguished
from rebuilding that C oracle. The primary wasm corpus has no such dependency.

| C archive | Audit |
|---|---|
| `fe_dump.cbor.zst`, `lsf_quant_io.cbor.zst` | front-end and LSF quantization/reconstruction |
| `pitchio_ground_truth.cbor.zst`, `sigmode_ground_truth.cbor.zst` | historical pitch/VUV profile |
| `gennoise_vectors.cbor.zst` | 41 cases selected across voiced/unvoiced/pulse/transition branches |
| `exc_pre_lags.cbor.zst`, `gennoise_params_dump.cbor.zst` | 156 records each; preserved packet groups |
| `pulse_vectors.cbor.zst`, `rc_vectors.cbor.zst` | pulse decode and additional range primitives |
| `e2e_vectors.cbor.zst` | historical energy-envelope regression corpus |
| `harm_postfilter_vectors.raw.zst` | complete stateful C harmonic-filter stream |
| `hp_postfilter_vectors.raw.zst` | 34 independently seeded C HP-filter cases |

The small `lsf_vectors.json`, `pitch_vectors.json`, `gains_vectors.json`, `vad_ground_truth.json`
and `toc_vectors.json` remain readable auditors. TOC's old escape-duration column is intentionally
ignored for `0xC0..=0xFF`; the dedicated writer/parser test covers those durations. No oracle data
was edited to remove that discrepancy.

The existing C packet/PCM pairs (`inbound_capture_frames.json`, `ref_usesmpl_expected.raw`,
`mlow_120ms_frames.json`, `ref_120ms_expected.raw`, `mlow_dtx_off_frames.json`,
`ref_dtx_off_expected.raw`) remain independent compatibility checks. The 120 ms/DTX-off C pairs
can also be regenerated with `MLOW_REFERENCE=/path/to/opus_mlow cargo xt mlow c-reference`.
Runtime seed tables are documented separately in [README.md](README.md).

## Verification

Local validation on 2026-09-04: 2261 wacore library tests passed, including all 131 MLOW tests;
two pre-existing ignored tests stayed ignored. Workspace clippy and explicit voip-mlow clippy
passed with `-D warnings`. The tool passed 17 library tests and workspace clippy. All 11 derivations
were reproduced in two fresh output directories, and regenerated primary/audit archives were
checked. Postfilter output-state comparisons passed separately after being added.

`.github/workflows/mlow-derive.yml` checks the pinned tool, re-derives both captures, compares every
primary fixture and runs the MLOW tests. The tool has its own J/S capture-matrix workflow.

Successful remote runs: [tool J/S matrix](https://github.com/oxidezap/unwasm/actions/runs/33938645892)
and [consumer regeneration plus MLOW tests](https://github.com/oxidezap/whatsapp-rust/actions/runs/33938854330).
The 60 ms PCM check also requires exactly 960 samples for every one of the 110 packets; no
inactive packet is skipped for producing a different length. This additional assertion passed locally.
The full testdata directory is approximately 9.1 MB, down from 15.8 MB before this migration.
